text.p: These are the headlines for selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada's defence costs to jump: U.S. report lacks details, but NATO expansion could cost C$708-million over 12 years.
- Ottawa hospitals to merge, close: Report first of coming blitz.
- Maple Leaf Gardens stops short of apology: Officials offer only sympathy.
- 'Bloodless medicine' urged for Canada: Drugs, surgical innovations already reducing need for transfusions, forum said.
- Jiang pledges to retain market reforms: China's new leader defends Tainanmen Square crackdown in eulogy for Deng.
- Canada's debt rating raised: U.S. firm approves as lower deficits lead to 41-year-low in requirement for foreign capital.
- Mitsubishi plans drive into Canada: Japanese auto maker to open dealership network to sell four vehicle models.
- Chamber letter angers generics: CCC seeks money to fight changes in Drug Patent Act.
- American cancels Vancouver flights: Airport, Canadian potential losers.
- Unions, bank battle for shareholder vote: Top bankers lobby hard for institutions to vote down shareholder's plan. But unions urge their pension funds to back the changes.
- Court will decide on Transwest, Jordon bid.
